items.elicits: Comparison of 3/4 and 5/8 with a relational symbol, plus the student's own account of how she knows it, using a common denominator, a picture, or a benchmark such as one half (Part A instruction line).
Comparison of 2/3 and 7/12 with a relational symbol and the supporting reasoning for that symbol.
Comparison of 5/6 and 8/9 with a relational symbol and the supporting reasoning for that symbol; the near-miss pair makes the choice of strategy visible in the written work.

components.claim_span: Chooses a valid strategy for comparing two unlike fractions
components.component: Selects one comparison approach for a pair of unlike fractions from the available approaches
components.evidence: Part A: "Then show how you know (a common denominator, a picture, or a benchmark like ½)." The item names three approaches and leaves the selection to the student.

components.component: Carries the chosen approach through to a comparison result and writes the symbol
components.evidence: Part A: "For each pair, write `<`, `>`, or `=`." Items 1-3 each require the carried-out comparison to produce the symbol.

components.claim_span: shows the reasoning that supports the symbol
components.component: Writes out the reasoning that connects the work to the symbol chosen
components.evidence: Part A: "Then show how you know", reinforced by the header instruction "Show all work".

coverage.why: Each move named in G5C1 - selecting an approach, carrying it out, and writing the reasoning behind the symbol - is asked for explicitly by the Part A instruction line and is exercised by items 1, 2 and 3.

conditions_support.conditions_reason: Supervision is declared "unsupervised" with an AI assistant and the internet permitted over a week, so the returned page shows a comparison and a written justification whose author cannot be established.
conditions_support.conditions_supports: A teacher may conclude from this work what a student can produce on unlike-fraction comparisons - symbol plus supporting reasoning - when working at home over a week with the internet and an AI assistant available.

intended_inference.why: The conditions block declares purpose "summative" and grouping "individual", and records that the teacher needs to conclude that each student individually can do what the claim names.

materiality.why: Nothing G5C1 names is left unasked, so there is no coverage limit to be material; the attribution limit is material because the inference the teacher declared is precisely the individual, independent one that unsupervised administration with a permitted AI assistant leaves open.

claims.conditions_missing_evidence: The declared conditions leave unestablished that the strategy choice, the execution and the written reasoning on the returned page originated with the student named at the top of it.
claims.narrower_inference: Each student can turn in a correct unlike-fraction comparison with a strategy and supporting reasoning when working at home with the internet and an AI assistant permitted.
claims.supports: That this assessment asks for the whole of G5C1 and returns work showing a chosen strategy, its execution, and reasoning tied to the symbol, produced under home conditions with resources available.
does_not_support: That any individual student chose and executed the comparison strategy without outside or machine help.
That the written reasoning on the page is the student's own account of her own thinking.
A summative individual judgment that a given student can compare unlike fractions unaided.

delegation.reason: Every part of items 1-3, including the written justification, is the kind of output a permitted AI assistant can produce in full, and the AI policy is declared "permitted".

claims.gap_statement: This assessment asks for everything G5C1 names, but under the declared unsupervised, AI-permitted conditions the resulting work cannot be attributed to the individual student, which is exactly the attribution the declared summative purpose requires.
claims.over_verified_note: Three separate comparison items exercise the same three components; on the coverage side this claim is repeatedly evidenced rather than thinly evidenced.

components.component: Adds, subtracts, or orders the parts once they are the same size
components.evidence: Part B heading "Add and subtract" with items 4-6, the Part C word problems 7 ("How far did she run in all") and 8 ("How much more flour"), and the Part A comparisons 1-3.

conditions_support.conditions_reason: The declared supervision is "unsupervised" with an AI assistant, the internet and anything at home permitted, and the procedure this claim names is exactly what those permitted tools carry out, so the step-by-step work returned cannot be attributed to the student.
conditions_support.conditions_supports: A teacher may conclude what a student turns in on multi-step unlike-denominator computation - including simplest form and mixed-number regrouping - when working at home over a week with calculators, the internet and an AI assistant available.

materiality.why: There is no coverage limit to weigh; the attribution limit is material because a procedural claim of this kind is the single most directly delegable thing on the page, and the declared inference is about the individual student's own execution.

claims.conditions_missing_evidence: The declared conditions leave unestablished that the common-denominator construction, the combination step and the simplification or regrouping shown on the page were carried out by the student.
claims.narrower_inference: Each student can submit correct, fully stepped unlike-denominator computation, in simplest form and regrouped to a mixed number where asked, when working at home with tools and an AI assistant permitted.
claims.supports: That the assessment asks for the whole of G5C2 across nine items and returns fully worked procedure produced under home conditions with resources available.

claims.gap_statement: Coverage of G5C2 is complete and repeated, but the declared unsupervised, AI-permitted administration leaves the procedure unattributable to the individual student the summative purpose is about.

items.elicits: An explanation of what the student who wrote 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/6 did wrong - the item presents the added-denominators error itself - together with the correct sum.

components.claim_span: States why adding denominators produces a wrong-sized part
components.component: Writes an account of what goes wrong when denominators are added
components.evidence: Item 9: "A student added 1/2 + 1/4 and got 2/6. Explain what the student did wrong" - the presented error is precisely the added-denominator error, and the item calls for the explanation of it.

components.component: Produces the correct result of the addition that was done wrongly

coverage.why: Item 9 asks for both moves the claim names and no more than them: the explanation of the added-denominator error and the correct sum. A single item exercising a component is exercise of it.

conditions_support.conditions_reason: Supervision is declared "unsupervised" with an AI assistant permitted, and this claim's observable is a short written explanation - the form of output most readily supplied by a permitted assistant - so the explanation on the page cannot be attributed to the student.
conditions_support.conditions_supports: A teacher may conclude what explanation of the added-denominator error a student is able to assemble and hand in when working at home with the internet and an AI assistant available.

intended_inference.why: The declared summative, individual framing means the teacher needs to conclude that each student individually holds the understanding this diagnostic claim names.

materiality.why: Nothing the claim names goes unasked, so coverage carries no limit; the attribution limit is material because a diagnostic claim about a student's own understanding of an error depends entirely on the explanation being hers.

claims.conditions_missing_evidence: The declared conditions leave unestablished that the explanation of the wrong-sized part, and the correct sum beside it, came from the student rather than from a permitted resource.
claims.narrower_inference: Each student can hand in a written account of the added-denominator error together with the correct sum when working at home with an AI assistant and the internet permitted.
claims.supports: That the assessment asks for both parts of G5C3 in item 9 and returns a written explanation and a correct sum produced under home conditions with resources available.
does_not_support: That an individual student can state, unaided, why adding denominators produces a wrong-sized part.
That the wording of the explanation reflects the student's own grasp of the error.
A summative individual diagnosis of who does and does not still hold this misconception.

delegation.reason: A written explanation of a named arithmetic error plus the correct sum is fully within what the declared permitted AI assistant produces on request.

claims.gap_statement: Item 9 asks for exactly what G5C3 names, but under the declared unsupervised, AI-permitted conditions the explanation cannot be attributed to the individual student, which is what a diagnostic claim under a summative purpose requires.

conditions_echo: Grade 5 mathematics, Unit 4 end-of-unit summative, sent home over a week; supervision unsupervised; individual work; AI policy permitted; resources permitted are anything at home, the internet and an AI assistant; time not stated; teacher's novelty note: students have practised this kind of item but these particular numbers and problems are new to them; the teacher requires individual, independent attribution.
reviewer_notes: Coverage and conditions diverge sharply and identically across all three claims. On coverage, this is a well-matched instrument: every component named in G5C1, G5C2 and G5C3 is asked for by name in the assessment, and the first two claims are exercised several times over. The novelty condition also holds on the teacher's own account - the particular numbers and problems are new. The single condition that fails is independence: unsupervised administration with an AI assistant permitted means none of the returned work is an observation of a student, so all three claims carry a conditions limitation and none carries a coverage limitation. That limitation is not a defect in the task - a take-home task can be a good take-home task, and work produced with these resources is real evidence of what students can produce with them; it is simply not evidence of the individual, unaided performance the declared summative purpose asks about.
